topic: Building in public as a solo founder solving everyday problems

post.topic: Building in public as a solo founder solving everyday problems
post.linkedin_text:
Stop building apps nobody asked for.

At JAEXS Solutions, we focus on a simple rule: find a real everyday problem first, then code the solution.

Too many developers fall in love with complex tech stacks instead of usable products.

→ Talk to real users.
→ Validate the pain point.
→ Write the simplest working code.

Building in public keeps you honest. You share the messy bugs, the pivot decisions, and the actual progress.

How do you usually find your project ideas?

slides.title: Stop building *random apps* nobody asked for
slides.body: How to find real problems to solve as a developer.

slides.title: Look for friction
slides.body: Notice repetitive manual tasks in your daily routine. If it annoys you, it probably annoys others too.

slides.title: Validate before coding
slides.body: Talk to people before opening your IDE. Make sure the pain point is real and worth solving.

slides.title: Build in public
slides.body: Share your progress, bugs, and lessons. Transparency builds trust long before your product launches.
